tasks.content: Designed the initial magneto-photoluminescence measurement strategy for resolving sub-percent field-dependent PL changes, including excitation-power monitoring, reference normalization, lock-in alternatives, repeated measurements, null tests, and common-power comparison.

Implemented Python 3.14 QEPro acquisition through seabreeze, including real and emulated spectrometer adapters, integration time, averaging, correction flags, signal-limit warnings, feature/capability probing, TEC access, device-averaging probing, and spectrum metadata.

Implemented Newport 2936-R USB control through pythonnet and Newport PowerMeterCommands.dll, including device discovery, channel selection, validated power/status reads, wavelength query/set, emulator support, live and spectra-only modes, bounded trace storage, statistics, trace export, and full-run logging.

Built the initial PySide6/pyqtgraph spectroscopy GUI with spectrum viewing, monitor plots, device emulators, file open/save, autosave, generated filenames, run identifiers, notes, keyboard shortcuts, persistent QSettings preferences, and configurable plot styles.

Refactored monolithic GUI code into panels, dialogs, controllers, device adapters, planning modules, IO modules, validation modules, and shared core records/settings. Extracted AcquisitionPanel, MonitorPanel, PowerPanel, LaserPanel, FilterWheelPanel, ScanPanel, and supporting dialogs.

Implemented Coherent OBIS Laser Box communication and emulation, including real/auto/emulated modes, connection refresh, per-laser enable/disable and setpoint control, CDRH-delay control, channel-1-through-5 Laser Box addressing, resilient Disable All behavior, wavelength swatches, and compact power formatting.

Implemented setpoint and calibrated laser power scans with linear/log/custom spacing, repeats, settling delays, scan metadata, warnings for clipped points, hard failures for invalid or out-of-range points, calibration-curve save/load, expected-actual-power interpolation, and autosaved scan spectra.

Implemented manual ND-filter-wheel definitions, nominal transmission calculation, dynamic programming to minimize filter changes, filter-aware scan previews, manual filter-change prompts, and filter-state metadata in saved spectra.

Implemented monitor improvements including scalar runtime history, integrated/peak/power-normalized metrics, bounded memory warnings, 2D field-power maps, optional OpenGL 3D views, persistent spectrum axis limits, and plot redraw throttling.

Hardened the repository with valid README.md and pyproject.toml, JSON lab defaults, batch startup modes, lazy hardware imports, scan-plan validation, Newport status-word decoding, atomic data exports, and repository hygiene fixes.

Decoupled spectrometer and power-meter connection states so either instrument can operate independently, added Instrument Connections controls, dynamic panel visibility, reconnect/disconnect operations, offline spectrum-viewer behavior, and suppression of optional operations when hardware is unavailable.

Completed a large code audit and refactor on the refactor/gui-cleanup branch: reduced MainWindow responsibilities, added InstrumentRuntime, ScanCoordinator, FileIOController, PreferencesController, SpectrumPanel, monitor-view helpers, processing modules, protocols, atomic IO, and 36 hardware-independent tests.

Replaced fixed live-acquisition polling with event-driven chaining, implemented independent spectrum/monitor/power redraw intervals, added redraw signals and PerformanceMonitor telemetry, and exposed persistent display/performance settings.

Implemented robust SNR estimation and CSV metadata, including baseline fitting, MAD noise estimation, peak and integrated SNR, detector-utilization reporting, configurable evaluation intervals, persisted SNR settings, and a recommendation dialog for integration time and averaging.

Added Visual Studio Dark styling, improved checkbox visibility, persistent theme selection, quick restart support, theme semantic models/catalog/rendering, preview/editor infrastructure, and display/performance/SNR settings dialogs.
Created the refactor/gui-cleanup Git branch and established a shared F:\ spectrometer GUI virtual environment for the original and refactored working trees.
Implemented initial software-timed gated-acquisition planning modules, gated metadata records, a gated acquisition panel/coordinator scaffold, and hardware-independent gated-sequence tests.

Created Andor capability probes for systems with Solis-installed native DLLs but no pyAndorSDK2/pyAndorSpectrograph wrappers, and established that atmcd64d.dll and atspectrograph.dll are present under C:\Program Files\Andor SOLIS.

Bench-validate the completed gated-acquisition integration on real hardware: software ownership, button-state wiring, acknowledgement/result routing, single autosave, persisted settings, absolute-delay metadata, abort behavior, and fail-safe laser disable are implemented; verify ON/OFF, delayed-after-OFF, and transition-series timing and saved-frame counts.

Implemented one common acquisition-sequence arbiter for manual, live, background, power/calibration scan, gated acquisition, and SNR auto-tuning ownership, with origin-specific result routing, composed panel state, stale-request rejection, and emergency Disable All coordination.

Bench-validate clean QEPro connection-loss, reconnect, and setting synchronization. SeaBreeze/USB transport normalization, centralized disconnect handling, the -20 to 40 C TEC guard, one read-only temperature health check after a TEC transfer error, and recoverable command-error handling are implemented. The 2026-09-02 candidate additionally clears every completed data-buffer frame and consumes one possible in-flight frame after integration, averaging, or correction changes. Hardware validation remains: reject -40 C without USB disruption, verify the first delivered frame after 1000 ms to 10 ms and averaging/correction changes uses the new settings, verify unchanged settings have no ongoing discard penalty, and confirm a real unplug produces one disconnected transition.

Completed the consolidated Andor ctypes probe on the lab computer using the empirically correct 64-bit SDK2 library atmcd64d_legacy.dll. The probe enumerated one DU401_BVF camera, serial 26970, with 1024 x 127 pixels and 26 um pixel pitch; queried temperature, capabilities, readout modes, amplifier/speed data, and clean shutdown; and independently enumerated Kymera serial KY-4444 and all four gratings. The prior zero-camera result was caused by selecting atmcd64d.dll rather than atmcd64d_legacy.dll.

Complete and harden production Andor support. Native SDK2 camera, ATSpectrograph/Kymera, combined Andor spectrometer, capability-driven controls, camera-to-spectrograph geometry transfer, and basic GUI acquisition now work with the DU401_BVF through atmcd64d_legacy.dll. Remaining work includes functional DLL fallback/configuration, full blocked-light and calibrated-spectrum regression, safe cooler shutdown, real readout/control validation, DU490A InGaAs enumeration and detector switching, and verified Kymera output-port/detector/calibration mapping.

Bench-validate the completed theme integration. The 2026-09-02 source caches a native System Default widget rendering before the persisted application stylesheet is applied, so preview widgets no longer inherit the active custom theme. Re-test the cached System preview at the lab display scale along with coupled selection/preview, custom themes, visible separators, persistence, and Apply & Restart.

Bench-test the completed SNR automatic-acquisition workflow against QEPro and emulators: coordinator wiring, fresh verification frames under current SNR settings, bounded integration/averaging adjustments, selected metric/tolerance, abort, repetition detection, and iteration/limit states are implemented.

Finish Newport acquisition decoupling and quantitative exposure association. Newport now has an independent worker/thread and optional before-spectrum-after routing no longer shares the spectrometer worker, but complete exposure-synchronous or timestamped ring-buffer statistics (mean, RMS, peak-to-peak, slope, valid count, rejected count) and real-hardware throughput validation remain.

Benchmark OceanDirect high-speed/device averaging and buffered acquisition on the QEPro, then decide whether to add OceanDirect as an optional spectrometer backend while retaining seabreeze as the stable default.

Bench-validate background subtraction as an explicit, reproducible processing path. Schema v2 now preserves canonical adapter-output counts separately from displayed/processed values, and live subtraction requires a strict stable signature covering backend/detector identity, wavelength grid/calibration, instrument state, correction flags, averaging, and integration. Dedicated mismatch handling is implemented. Remaining work is real-detector validation and a decision on whether a separately validated rate-scaled policy should ever be added.

Implement processing/analysis modules for spectral-template amplitude fitting, shift/baseline separation, PL versus measured power fitting/interpolation, common-power magneto-PL calculation, drift/null/Allan stability diagnostics, uncertainty estimates, and live/offline analysis views.

Add experiment-consistency scan options: randomized or bidirectional power order, repeated reference-power insertion, pre/post zero-field blocks, settling/discard frames after manual changes, null-difference analysis, and minimum-SNR/quality warnings.

Add phosphorescence workflows for Kymera or QEPro: continuous/kinetic acquisition around laser-off transitions, decay metadata and fitting, timing-jitter reporting, and optional Thorlabs SH05 shutter control once the exact shutter-controller model is identified.

Add optional spectral-response correction using a user-supplied calibrated system-response curve while always retaining raw counts; document the QEPro-FL grating/detector/slit/order-sorting configuration and response-calibration procedure.

Package the stabilized GUI as a Windows standalone application, starting with a PyInstaller one-directory build, including config/theme resources while relying on installed vendor drivers, then create an installer after QEPro/Newport/OBIS/Andor validation.

Complete a full real-instrument regression of the merged 2026-09-02 candidate. Source fixes now cover System Default preview isolation, QEPro TEC/stale-buffer behavior, instrument-disconnect state propagation, Newport process-isolated hot reconnect, GUI-first expected errors, and invalid filename tokens. Bench validation remains for those paths, while OBIS physical-key/interlock truth and fail-safe optical state remain unresolved safety work. Repeat startup/shutdown/reconnect tests under partial hardware availability before declaring the release validated.
Consider future SR830/lock-in integration with a dedicated photodetector and optional monochromator/filter metadata, while keeping QEPro software-demodulation as a separate slow spectral mode.

Completed the 2026-08-19 source-level engineering audit and offline refactor: sequence arbitration and deterministic result routing, scan/gated laser fail-safe exits, QEPro disconnect normalization, lossless spectrum/power CSV metadata, theme/persistence cleanup, Andor probe consolidation/correction, import-safe diagnostics, packaging asset discovery, documentation, and hardware-independent regression coverage.

Consolidate USB version control: import the spectrometer-gui-reviewed source snapshot as a history-preserving review/2026-08-19-reviewed branch based on current main, move machine-specific settings to config/lab_defaults.local.json, inspect omitted tracked files and all untracked/ignored data, run the outstanding real-hardware regression, merge and tag only after validation, then remove redundant refactor/reviewed directories after confirming they contain no unique work.

Bench-validate unified transport-loss normalization and connection-state propagation for QEPro, Newport, and OBIS devices. The source closes/removes a confirmed-lost adapter, stops only its polling, aborts dependent acquisition ownership safely, emits one machine-readable disconnected transition, disables/hides associated controls, and keeps offline spectrum viewing available. OBIS key/interlock truth remains separate safety work.

Completed power-meter disconnect presentation and automatic filename cleanup: the toolbar power QWidgetAction and dependent panel/controls are hidden when Newport is unavailable, stale label text is cleared, and nonfinite optional power or magnetic-field values are omitted from generated filenames instead of producing tokens such as nan_W.

Bench-validate Newport 2936-R hot reconnect after a power cycle. The focused reconnect probe now compares repeated reconstruction in one Python/CLR process with reconstruction in fresh child processes and records PnP/assembly/device evidence. The GUI now isolates pythonnet, the vendor assembly, device key, and meter object in a restartable spawned helper process; startup performs one quick optional-hardware probe, while an explicit reconnect performs five fresh-process attempts with bounded delays. Return the diagnostic JSON if fresh-process recovery still fails.

Harden OBIS Laser Box control around the physical key/interlock and power loss. Normalize pyserial failures including timeout reconfiguration, distinguish requested state from verified emission readiness, query supported status/interlock indicators, clear any unverified latched ON request, expose disconnected/interlocked/verified states in the GUI, and require verified readiness for scan and gated workflows.

Diagnose the lab computer popup "Please insert the last disk of the Multi-Volume set" that recurs on USB device events. Quarantine and test split/corrupt ZIP archives, disable AutoPlay for isolation, back up the removable drive, run a read-only filesystem scan, and confirm whether the trigger is Windows Explorer rather than GUI instrument communication.

Completed the Andor probe and adapter refinements: corrected the Kymera focal-length units to 0.328 m / 328 mm, distinguished successful-but-unconfigured standalone spectrograph pixel geometry from camera failure, enumerated the DU401_BVF through atmcd64d_legacy.dll, obtained 1024 x 127 and 26 um detector geometry, transferred geometry into the production Kymera calibration path, and successfully connected and acquired spectra through the GUI. Multi-detector validation remains under the broader production Andor task.

Created a general Git workflow and command-reference manual covering repository initialization, prototype-to-canonical-directory cleanup, branching, fixed-workstation and removable-drive workflows, commit conventions, common command arguments and examples, and recovery recipes.

Established the standard workflow for integrating a standalone prototype directory into the tracked project: initialize the prototype as a branch anchored to origin/main with git reset --mixed so modifications, additions, and deletions are represented exactly; validate and merge through a pull request; then update the canonical checkout and remove the redundant prototype directory after auditing local-only files and unpushed commits.

Diagnosed the Andor iDus SDK2 discovery failure. Windows, Solis, and PyLabLib all identified the DU401_BVF; process-module inspection showed that PyLabLib loads C:\Program Files\Andor SOLIS\atmcd64d_legacy.dll. Reordering the project SDK2 candidates and the ctypes probe to prefer that library changed GetAvailableCameras from zero to one and enabled normal camera control and GUI measurements. The non-legacy atmcd64d.dll remains present but does not enumerate this legacy iDus installation.

Harden Andor SDK2 DLL selection. Explicit camera-DLL configuration, legacy-first selection, selected-DLL capability/connection reporting, camera-only probe scope, and an isolated-process DLL matrix diagnostic are implemented. The current lab default is atmcd64d_legacy.dll. Remaining work is a production functional fallback policy for other installations; do not load competing SDK2 runtimes sequentially in the GUI process, and never rename/replace Solis DLLs.

Bench-validated Newport hot reconnect through the restartable helper process on 2026-09-11. After a physical power cycle, the GUI successfully created a fresh spawned CLR/vendor process and reconnected to the meter. Keep troubleshooting/newport_reconnect_probe.py for regression evidence if the workstation or vendor runtime changes.

Bench-validated the GUI-first startup error policy on 2026-09-11: expected unavailable-instrument states appeared in the status bar without terminal warnings or tracebacks. Requested connection and handled operation failures remain concise GUI messages with optional rotating-file detail, while internal defects and uncaught failures remain terminal-visible. A separate UX task remains to make a missing config/lab_defaults.local.json file clearer to users.

Bench-validate spectrometer source selection. Auto/QEPro/Andor/emulator/disconnected are implemented in configuration, CLI, Windows launcher, and the session Instrument Connections dialog. Auto quietly tries the configured QEPro serial then Andor and starts offline when neither is present; Newport and laser choices remain independent. A chooser for the future case where both detectors are simultaneously visible and a remember-next-startup policy still require user input.

Implemented compact spectrum CSV schema_version=3. Closely related values are grouped on one line; an option value itself indicates enablement and False/None represents disablement where appropriate; canonical adapter output is always retained and processed output appears only when changed; normal Newport status, inactive workflow flags, duplicate notes encodings, and unrelated sentinels are omitted. Conditional acquisition, power, scan/laser/filter, background, gated, SNR, and identity groups remain round-trip compatible with schema-v1/v2 and two-column files. The complete parameter catalog and migration map are in docs/SPECTRUM_METADATA_SCHEMA_20260909.docx.

Bench-validate the implemented session-only laser selector. A compact Use checkbox exists at the left of each row; zero or one laser can be active; selecting another transfers choice; the active box clears on a second click; selection is keyed by port/channel and survives tabs, measurements, edits, and refresh while present; table hover/focus and emission buttons do not select; the choice is not persisted across GUI sessions.

Completed the compact acquisition-layout and smoothing follow-up. Exposure, averages, smoothing, field, live, take-spectrum, and background controls remain directly visible; corrections, averaging backend, power association, and related controls are grouped under Advanced. Smoothing now supports None, Boxcar, Hann, Hamming, Gaussian, Triangle, Blackman, Cosine, and Sine kernels with selectable nearest/reflect/wrap/constant boundaries, an inline kernel preview, and a detailed Fourier popup. Savitzky-Golay remains deliberately deferred until its parameter semantics are approved.

Verify controller-to-UI import decoupling when merging this candidate against commit aeca6f0. The available reviewed source uses postponed annotations/duck-typed panel dependencies and has no runtime AcquisitionPanel, FilterWheelPanel, LaserPanel, or ScanPanel imports in controllers/scan_coordinator.py. The exact current GitHub source was unavailable, so confirm/remove any imports introduced only upstream and rerun import/coordinator tests.

Unified laser-calibration and power-dependent scan repetition control. One Repeats per point widget now supplies both workflows, and the separate calibration reads/point widget and persistence key were intentionally removed. Do not reintroduce the removed control; the shared behavior is the required design.

Restored repository configuration hygiene. Tracked defaults and examples are generic, machine-local Newport DLL paths, serials, and ports belong in ignored config/lab_defaults.local.json, and the documented override path preserves independent instrument selection.

Bench-characterize the optimized gated timing path. Planning/preflight/preview are lazy and bounded; settings and reusable detector state are prepared before timing; Newport/frame defaults are off; the coordinator uses perf_counter_ns absolute deadlines and Qt PreciseTimer no-early rechecks; adapters return best-available acquisition bounds; an online robust exposure-aware guard flags individual outliers, discards averaged outliers, and aborts excessive inconsistency; averaged files include timing distributions plus pump/frame/repeat gaps. Andor Run-Till-Abort is now implemented to remove per-frame re-arm overhead. Remaining work is GUI/hardware validation of frame freshness and order, threshold tuning, photodiode/TTL validation, FIRE/strobe/external-trigger calibration, and hardware triggering for time scales software cannot resolve.

Merge the 2026-09-02 validation candidate against GitHub main aeca6f0995764b430bee7872b363893e7a4bf4f2 (or newer) before deployment. The review environment could verify the commit/timestamp through the project ledger but could not download the private current tree; preserve unique upstream changes and machine-local configuration, confirm the shared repeats-per-point design, then run Python 3.14 pytest and the ordered lab checklist in REVIEW_20260902.md.

Bench-validate QEPro buffer synchronization. The adapter now detects changes to integration, requested/applied averaging, and correction flags, clears every completed SeaBreeze data_buffer element when available, discards one possible in-flight frame, and returns only the next spectrum. Verify 1000 ms to 10 ms and averaging/correction changes with a stable lamp; unchanged settings must not incur repeated discard or throughput loss.

Resolved the product decisions in Spectrometer_GUI_Questions_20260902_answered.docx. Record field applicability, bounded default logging, single-visible spectrometer auto-selection, strict background compatibility, abnormal-only power status, compact Advanced-layout direction, initial smoothing kernels/preview, online robust gated rejection, guided Andor cooler shutdown direction, and tracked-versus-local configuration are now durable requirements. Implemented items and deferred items are split into dated follow-up tasks.

Completed magnetic-field metadata applicability. Record field is persisted, controls whether field metadata and filename tokens are emitted, disables the value control when unchecked, and treats 0 mT as a valid recorded value rather than missing. Field values propagate as float-or-None through acquisition, gated averaging, monitoring, naming, and schema-v3 export; regression tests cover unchecked, zero, and nonzero cases.

Replaced eager gated plan construction with an O(1)-allocation lazy sequence and compact preview/preflight summaries. Added exact action/frame counts, 100000-frame and 250000-action hard guards, a 5000-trace averaged-output guard, a 512 MiB estimated-memory warning, explicit repeat gaps, friendly mode labels, repeat xN preview rows, and disabling of delay-step input when only one frame is requested. A 100000-frame plan builds in about 0.27 ms with about 1.7 KiB traced peak allocation in the review runtime.

Implemented bounded online gated timing-quality control without retaining all spectra. After warm-up it uses rolling robust median/MAD-IQR residual statistics, exposure uncertainty as a lower bound, and an outlier-fraction abort rule. The answered policy is now automatic: individual-frame outputs retain and flag timing outliers, while averaged outputs discard them. Baselines are separated by spectrometer backend and gated mode, stable bias warns without discarding, user abort saves an accepted partial average without a failure flag, and non-user failures retain an incomplete reason. Incremental averaging keeps mean/M2 plus compact timing statistics, and the coordinator prepares settings and detector streaming before the time-sensitive laser transition.

Bench-tune and validate the gated timing rejection policy on both QEPro and iDus. The policy decisions are fixed: flag individual outputs, discard averaged outliers, separate rolling baselines by backend and gated mode, warn only for stable bias, save accepted partial averages on user abort without marking them failed, and retain a failure reason for non-user termination. Confirm the five-sample warm-up, 4.5-sigma multiplier, exposure-derived uncertainty floor, and abort above 25 percent after ten evaluations. Use optical/TTL timing evidence rather than SDK call bounds alone.

Added acquisition progress reporting for long exposures and averaging. Adapters emit per-average progress, the controller/runtime forwards it, MainWindow owns one status-bar progress bar, and the status text reports Acquisition N/M. The bar appears for at least 10 averages or an estimated acquisition of at least 0.5 s and is reset on completion/failure/cancellation.

Bench-validate the new acquisition progress UI under PySide6: one long exposure, 100 software averages, device averaging, cancellation, failure, live acquisition, background, scan, and gated ownership. Confirm no stale bar, no excessive signal overhead, and correct Acquisition N/M text.

Analyzed the completed iDus timing probes at 15 ms/50 frames and 50 ms/1000 frames across all four vertical speeds. DU401_BVF serial 26970 reports 1024 by 127 pixels at 26 um, horizontal rates 0.1/0.05/0.033 MHz, and vertical shifts 8.25/16.25/32.25/64.25 us. Run-Till-Abort sustained approximately 15.00 ms or 50.00 ms frame periods with sub-0.2 ms standard deviation, while re-armed acquisition required roughly 117-200 ms per frame and transfer itself was below 0.1 ms. This identifies SDK2 per-frame re-arming as the dominant former GUI bottleneck and does not justify a Python/C++ rewrite.

Implemented SDK2 Run-Till-Abort circular-buffer acquisition for Andor Live, repeated manual/rapid acquisition, gated acquisition, power scans, and auto-tuning through explicit continuous-session identifiers. The adapter arms once per compatible settings/session, drains frames completed before the request, waits for and removes the oldest fresh frame, records driver index/discarded backlog/pending depth, detects invalid ranges or overwrite, and aborts/restores single-scan state on settings changes, ownership end, errors, disconnect, or shutdown. Gated preparation arms the stream before the laser transition.

Implemented guided Andor cooler shutdown using the answered policy. Normal close stops acquisition and hazardous outputs, turns the cooler off, displays progress, and queries temperature on a two-second timer until the detector reaches at least 0 C. Ordinary close remains blocked during warm-up; a clearly confirmed emergency override preserves a persistent incomplete-shutdown marker, and next startup warns while also querying the actual camera state. The default TEC target is 0 C. Bench evidence is still required to decide whether the threshold needs a hold period.

Implemented the answered compact acquisition-panel design and generalized smoothing. High-frequency controls remain visible in compact rows; corrections, averaging backend, power association, and related controls are in Advanced. Nine smoothing choices and four edge-boundary modes are persisted and round-trip through schema v4, with an inline kernel preview and a detailed Fourier popup. Savitzky-Golay remains deferred pending parameter semantics.

Completed extension design documentation. docs/EXTENSIBILITY_AND_PROCEDURES_20260909.docx defines plugins, declarative procedures, trusted Python extensions, external API alternatives, recommended hybrid architecture, capability contracts, safety boundaries, lifecycle, phased roadmap, and acceptance tests. No runtime plugin or procedure execution was added in this review.

After the trust model and first pilot are approved, introduce typed capability/adapter contracts and a plugin registry with manifest validation, compatibility checks, enable/disable state, diagnostics, and no direct widget mutation. Recommended first pilot is a read-only magnetic-field sensor; recommended procedure v1 is a bounded declarative YAML/JSON DSL with emulator dry-run, validation, resource locking, cancellation, and audit logs.

Updated ARCHITECTURE.md with concrete UI/controller/runtime/device/planning/processing/IO communication pathways, major methods, acquisition ownership, gated execution state, data flow, invariants, and the future extension boundary. Added REVIEW_20260909.md, full metadata schema/migration documentation, extension/procedure feasibility documentation, and a fillable next-step questions document.

Run the ordered Python 3.14/PySide6/vendor-driver lab checklist in REVIEW_20260909.md before replacing the lab branch. Highest priority: Andor Run-Till-Abort frame freshness/order and 1/5/10 ms applied-exposure matrix; one blocked-light gated run per backend; timing-guard threshold characterization; cooler warm-up/marker behavior; long-acquisition progress; QEPro stale-buffer synchronization; Newport process restart recovery and channel selection; partial-hardware startup; background-throughput regression; smoothing preview/theme rendering; and schema-v4 CSV round trips in the normal analysis workflow.

Bench-revalidate Andor Run-Till-Abort integration after the 2026-09-11 stale-notification fix. Exercise Live, a power scan, auto-tuning, and every gated mode; change integration/readout/binning between sessions; stop/cancel/reconnect; deliberately let the circular buffer accumulate; and verify returned driver indices are ordered, every pre-request frame is discarded, stale waits recover, overflow becomes a structured error, no stale frame crosses a settings or owner boundary, and metadata reports run_till_abort with correct discarded/pending counts. Ordinary manual Take Spectrum remains a single-scan path.

Run the blocked-light Andor short-exposure matrix at requested 1, 5, and 10 ms for the available readout/vertical-speed combinations. Confirm SDK2 applied exposure and frame period, verify saved integration_ms is the applied value and integration_requested_ms appears only on mismatch, then decide whether the GUI should constrain requests below a measured configuration-specific floor.

Bench-validate guided iDus cooler shutdown and startup recovery. Confirm cooler-OFF command/readback, two-second progress updates, normal close at the first reading at or above 0 C, emergency override confirmation, persistence and later clearing of the incomplete marker, behavior after process/USB failure, and whether lab practice or vendor guidance requires consecutive readings or a hold interval.

Bench-validate Newport channel selection and wrong-channel warnings. Test channel 1, channel 2, and both during single, averaged, live, scan, and gated spectra; verify at least one channel is required when Measure power is active; confirm only selected physical channels are saved and loaded in the same positions; tune the configurable imbalance threshold and consecutive-count warning without auto-switching channels.

Bench-validated the background-subtraction performance correction on 2026-09-11. With subtraction active, visible Live throughput was approximately the same as acquisition without subtraction. The implementation uses vectorized subtraction, cached grid/settings signatures, asynchronous serialized autosave, and fast-decaying performance-lag reporting. A separate UX task remains because the persisted subtraction checkbox can be checked before an in-memory background exists.

Implemented compact schema_version=4 spectrum and gated-series output. Records now include approved software provenance, readback-confirmed Andor optical/readout state, continuous-buffer timing, selected Newport channel identities, strict background signature, smoothing method/width/boundary, pump and repetition gaps, and equivalent provenance on one-file gated averages. Redundant inactive flags, normal power status, repeated background parameters, duplicate notes encodings, and always-duplicated processed arrays remain removed; schema-v1 through v4 loading remains supported.

After approving measured-field metadata, implement the first read-only field_sensor.v1 adapter/plugin pilot. Keep manual Record field semantics distinct from measured value, source identity, timestamp/age, and uncertainty; do not add these proposed fields to production spectrum metadata until the schema decision is explicit.

Benchmark detector-temperature query latency and choose a maximum acceptable reading age before adding temperature/cooler fields to spectrum metadata. Recommended initial policy is cached sampling only when exposure or total averaging time exceeds one second, contingent on negligible measured overhead.

Diagnosed the production Andor multi-frame failure from the complete 2026-09-11 lab log. SDK2 WaitForAcquisitionTimeOut returned success after the GUI freshness drain, but GetOldestImage then returned DRV_NO_NEW_DATA. This is consistent with a stale notification or short event-to-buffer driver race. The adapter now requires GetNumberNewImages to confirm unread data, ignores false-ready successful waits within the original timeout, records their count diagnostically, and has a deterministic regression for the drain/event/new-frame sequence.

The core Andor Run-Till-Abort retest passed: andor_stream_gap_probe completed 100/100 requests at 15 ms with a 100 ms gap, indices were monotonic from 1 to 694, 594 pre-request frames were discarded, and 99 stale notifications recovered; GUI Live and multi-frame gated acquisition also passed. Complete the remaining power-scan, auto-tune, explicit multi-average, stop/cancel/reconnect, and deliberate-overflow cases before closing the broader multi-owner regression.

Diagnosed and corrected the stable negative gated exposure-midpoint bias in all three supplied Kymera CSV files. The values were not caused by timer reset or saving: the stream returned a frame whose readout completed after the request even though its exposure midpoint preceded the target by approximately 9.4 to 11.5 ms. Gated OFF-frame requests now carry an absolute midpoint target into SDK2; the adapter dates the oldest pending frame, discards early candidates under one bounded deadline, and records target-alignment discards separately from pre-request backlog.

Completed the midpoint-alignment retest from the 2026-09-14 archive. Both gap probes completed 100/100 requests with monotonic indices. The unaligned run had all 99 steady-state exposure midpoints early; the aligned run had all 99 eligible and recorded 198 target discards. In the eight GUI files, negative means/minima were confined to zero-delay exposure starts while accepted exposure midpoints, request/call values, and timing-error means were nonnegative.

Implemented a transactional Andor Spectrometer Details path. A pinned Apply and verify action captures edits before disabling controls, the device worker stops the retained stream, validates and applies camera/Kymera changes in safe order, waits for available motor readback, refreshes calibration/capabilities, and returns explicit success or retryable failure to the open dialog. Added troubleshooting/andor_controls_probe.py, which is read-only by default and restores explicitly authorized changes unless --keep-changes is supplied.

Completed the 2026-09-14 reversible Andor control matrix. Grating, center wavelength, Kymera filter, flipper, horizontal speed, vertical speed, and available preamp gain applied and restored. Unavailable gain index 2 was rejected before native mutation. FVB binning 4 returned DRV_NOT_SUPPORTED and focus 423 to 400 returned ATSPECTROGRAPH_P2INVALID; follow-up tasks narrow the GUI and resolve those two capabilities rather than treating the matrix as a silent success.

Persist the successful iDus TEC target visually for the current GUI session. AndorSDK2Camera now caches a successfully applied target and exposes it through the capability schema, so reopening Spectrometer Details no longer resets the target widget while the connected camera remains at the previous setpoint.

Next functional fix after the Andor control and midpoint retests: eliminate duplicate iDus cooler-warning/confirmation windows, suppress the cold-camera exit workflow during an application-controlled theme restart, and verify window X, cancel, normal warm-up close, and confirmed emergency exit each produce one coherent state transition.

Run the 1/5/10 ms Andor mode-5 exposure matrix and make the acquisition controls clearly show SDK-applied exposure when it differs from the request. CSV schema v4 already records applied integration as primary and the differing request conditionally; do not impose a configuration-specific minimum until the mode-5 evidence is available.

Resolve remaining non-blocking GUI issues after the functional Andor work: prioritize acquisition progress over transient laser/status messages; improve progress placement; explain or disable persisted background subtraction until a background exists; clarify acquisition-time magnetic-field capture; normalize checkbox/label order and spacing; improve disabled checked-box contrast and dark spin arrows; repair cross-theme preview backgrounds or retire the redundant preview; and make missing local configuration explicit.

Implemented bounded Retain N inside fixed window timing for averaged delayed-after-OFF and interleaved-decay acquisitions. Repeats is the accepted target per trace; start or midpoint reference and symmetric tolerance are selectable; rejected arrays are released; complete pump/OFF attempts continue to a finite multiplier ceiling; partial accepted output survives failure; per-frame Newport I/O, individual output, and duplicate fixed-delay identities are prohibited.

Bench-validate fixed-window retention. Start with delayed-after-OFF at 10 ms, exposure midpoint, 20 accepted spectra, +/-8 ms, and a 3x ceiling. Verify exact retained/rejected/attempt accounting, no rejected contribution to averages, finite-ceiling partial save/failure reason, abort/disconnect cleanup, and laser OFF. Narrow the tolerance only after measuring retention yield.

Establish a physical laser timing reference with a fast photodiode and oscilloscope/DAQ or a characterized trigger/FIRE path. Measure command-to-optical OFF offset and jitter per OBIS box/channel. Current gated timestamps are process-monotonic software values referenced after serial command acknowledgement/readback completion, not optical edges; do not claim a physical +/- tolerance until calibrated.

Narrowed production Andor capabilities to lab-confirmed behavior. The FVB camera schema now advertises binning 1 only and rejects other values before native mutation. Kymera focus readback remains visible but its GUI editor is disabled after a reversible value returned ATSPECTROGRAPH_P2INVALID. The controls probe now emits its full capability schema for future range/contract diagnosis.

Resolve Kymera focus setter semantics/range around current readback 423 using vendor documentation and narrowly bounded reversible probes before re-enabling the GUI control. Keep FVB binning at 1 unless another verified SDK2 acquisition/read mode accepts larger binning, returns the correct array geometry, restores cleanly, and refreshes wavelength calibration.

Design and implement a low-light phase-cycled boxcar workflow after optical throughput is optimized: alternate matched pump/reference phases, pair-subtract spectra, accumulate mean and propagated variance, retain raw phase traces or sufficient audit evidence, and optionally add wavelength-band/template estimators. This is CCD synchronous detection, not an analog lock-in, and cannot replace insufficient photon collection.

memory.content: Project repository: https://github.com/cclark012/spectrometer-gui.git. Active development branch: refactor/gui-cleanup. Main entry point: gui.py. The refactored branch should remain separate from main until physical-instrument validation is complete.

Shared development virtual environment is located on the F:\ drive so both original and refactored worktrees can use the same interpreter. Virtual environments should be recreated rather than moved if embedded paths become invalid.

Current primary hardware: Ocean Insight QEPro-FL spectrometer; Newport 2936-R power meter controlled through PowerMeterCommands.dll/pythonnet; two Coherent OBIS Laser Boxes using virtual COM ports; Andor Kymera 328i with iDus DU401A-BVF CCD and DU490A-1.7 InGaAs detector; Sumitomo RDK-408D cryostat; Thorlabs SH05 shutter head with controller model still to be identified.

The lab computer has Andor Solis installed under C:\Program Files\Andor SOLIS. Native DLLs atmcd64d.dll and atspectrograph.dll are present, but pyAndorSDK2 and pyAndorSpectrograph are not installed. The next step is the corrected ctypes probe, followed by direct native wrappers.

OBIS Laser Box addressing convention: channel 0 is the box/controller and laser heads are channels 1 through 5. Never send SOURce0 laser commands. Full discovery should occur only at startup/refresh, not after each setpoint or enable command.

Newport status words are used to validate readings. Required-channel checks should reject missing detector, range-changing/unsettled, saturated, and overrange states; live invalid points are ignored/retried while spectrum-associated invalid reads should fail rather than save bad normalization.

Spectrometer and power meter connections are independent. Real mode should not silently fall back to emulators unless explicitly requested. When hardware is unavailable, relevant controls are hidden/disabled while the Spectrum viewer remains available for offline files.

The GUI is event-driven. Live acquisition is chained after completion rather than polled at a fixed 250 ms interval. Spectrum, monitor, and power redraws use independent dirty-flag timers and PerformanceMonitor reports acquisition rate, redraw rates, displayed/acquired fraction, and event-loop lag.

SNR estimation uses unsmoothed spectra, robust baseline/noise estimation, peak and integrated SNR, and detector full-scale utilization. SNR settings persist and are sent to the device worker at startup. The most recent valid SNR remains visible when evaluation is configured for every N spectra.

Power scans regenerate their plan immediately before Run. Impossible, nonfinite, calibration-out-of-range, or filter-infeasible points fail the plan; clipped setpoints generate visible warnings and require user confirmation. Scan spectra save requested power, laser setpoint, expected actual power, measured power, field, filter state, and acquisition metadata.

For quantitative magneto-PL, compare spectra at common measured Newport power rather than commanded OBIS setpoint. Primary planned metric is 100*(PL(B)-PL(0))/PL(0), using repeat averaging, power-response fitting/interpolation, reference points, null tests, fixed acquisition settings, and integrated/template-fit amplitudes rather than single noisy pixels.

Current live background subtraction is not trusted for experiments because it previously caused major GUI slowdown. Background spectra can be saved for offline subtraction until cached background-grid processing is validated.

Theme system direction: semantic ThemeDefinition JSON, catalog-backed ThemeManager, Visual Studio Dark as the current default, persistent selection, preview/editor support, quick restart to apply global theme changes, and Qt resources or Windows-safe absolute paths for checkbox SVG assets.

Gated/phosphorescence acquisition is software-timed on Windows. It is suitable initially for relatively slow decays and must save requested and observed transition timings; it is not deterministic microsecond gating. Hardware shutter integration requires the exact Thorlabs shutter controller model.

Standalone packaging should begin with PyInstaller one-directory mode after hardware backends stabilize. Vendor USB drivers, Andor/Ocean/Newport runtimes, and .NET components will still need to be installed on the host system.

User preferences: provide exact file locations for every suggested code change; keep responses structured, analytical, and concise; prefer code directly in chat unless a multi-file replacement or downloadable bundle is substantially more practical.

The 2026-08-19 reviewed bundle syntax-compiles all 115 Python files, passes 56 hardware-independent tests through a compatibility runner, imports all 98 non-test modules with optional dependency stubs, has no duplicate definitions, builds a wheel with required UI assets when Requires-Python is intentionally ignored under the available Python 3.12 environment, and passes git whitespace checks. PySide6 and vendor SDKs were unavailable, so these results do not replace Python 3.14 GUI or real-instrument validation.

Acquisition ownership is now exclusive and origin-aware. Automated frame requests that cannot be queued fail their requesting coordinator instead of hanging; scan/calibration abort and failure paths request laser disable; and Disable All aborts the owning state machine before the box-wide command so queued work cannot turn a laser back on.

Spectrum CSV now round-trips all SNR and gated-frame fields plus arbitrary note text without conflating literal backslash-n with line breaks. Power trace CSV retains point source, Newport command status, and every channel status word. Existing legacy spectrum CSV files remain readable.

USB repository consolidation strategy: keep one ordinary clone named spectrometer-gui as the canonical checkout. Avoid linked Git worktrees on the removable drive because changing drive letters can invalidate linked-worktree paths and require repair. The merged spectrometer-gui-refactor tree is redundant once unique local work is ruled out; spectrometer-gui-reviewed is a source-only snapshot that must be committed on a review branch before deletion. Keep machine-specific COM/DLL settings in ignored config/lab_defaults.local.json and keep experiment/calibration data outside repository directories.

The corrected Andor ctypes probe completed without a native crash. Kymera serial KY-4444 and four gratings were queried successfully and the JSON report was written. SDK2 reported zero available cameras; ATSpectrographGetPixelWidth and ATSpectrographGetNumberPixels returned success with zero values, indicating detector geometry has not yet been supplied to the spectrograph calibration path. The reported focal length value 0.328 is in metres and corresponds to the Kymera 328 mm focal length.

Real QEPro testing found that requesting an invalid TEC target such as -40 C can raise a SeaBreeze data-transfer error and interrupt GUI communication even though the device remains powered and reconnects successfully. The first spectrum after changing integration time can also be the previously buffered frame; subsequent spectra use the new integration time.

QEPro throughput was approximately 8-10 spectra/s while Newport power-meter reads shared the acquisition worker, versus approximately 90-100 spectra/s without the power meter. This strongly supports moving Newport acquisition to its own worker and associating timestamped power samples with each exposure from a bounded ring buffer.

Instrument disconnect state is not consistently propagated to the GUI. Associated controls can remain enabled after loss. Newport disconnect hides its panel but not the toolbar power label, nonfinite power creates nan_W filename tokens, and a power-cycled Newport does not currently reconnect through repeated refresh/connect attempts.

The OBIS Laser Box physical key/interlock can leave commanded and optical states desynchronized: an ON request issued while the key blocks emission may take effect when the key is later enabled. Refresh currently repairs the displayed state. A powered-off box can raise serial.serialutil.SerialException while pyserial reconfigures the timeout, before the existing query exception handling is entered.

System Default theme preview is not isolated from the application-level current theme: the plot changes explicitly, while preview widgets continue to inherit the applied theme. Use a cached native-system preview captured before applying the persisted theme or a fully isolated preview process/widget style context.

The lab computer repeatedly displays the Windows Compressed Folders multi-volume-set popup on USB device events. Treat this as an operating-system/archive or removable-media issue until isolated; quarantine split/corrupt archives and verify the USB filesystem before attributing it to instrument-query code.

GitHub main was verified at commit 5ea97aeeb7a88df0add189e9afddf06efac1dec1, committed 2026-08-20 14:21:28 at UTC-06:00. That commit omits nonfinite field and power tokens from automatic filenames. The immediately preceding changes hide the toolbar power label when Newport is absent, add only an unused ObisDisconnectedError stub, add independent scan power-unit widgets that still share the single scan/power_units settings key, and add a separate andor_ctypes_probe_fix.py alongside existing probes.

QEPro patch artifacts were prepared against main commit 5ea97ae. Changed files: devices/qepro_adapter.py, controllers/device_controller.py, and tests/test_qepro_adapter.py. The patch rejects nonfinite/out-of-guard TEC targets before USB, performs one CCD-temperature health check after a transport-class setpoint failure, preserves connection state when that check succeeds, caches applied integration/device-averaging settings, and discards exactly one frame after a configuration change. All 64 hardware-independent tests pass under Python 3.13; Python 3.14 and real-QEPro validation remain.

A reusable Git manual was created as Practical_Git_Project_Tracking_and_Command_Reference.docx. It is workflow-first, uses PowerShell-compatible examples, distinguishes fixed-location and USB repositories, emphasizes one canonical directory per active location, and includes destructive-command safeguards and recovery recipes.

For a standalone prototype with extensive tree changes and no history that must be retained, do not merge unrelated Git histories or manually reconcile duplicate folders. Initialize the prototype directory as a temporary repository, fetch origin/main, run git reset --mixed origin/main to preserve the prototype working tree while anchoring history to current main, commit the resulting snapshot on an integration branch, merge by pull request, update the one canonical checkout, and delete the temporary directory only after verifying it is clean and fully pushed.

The current Andor diagnostic strategy is to avoid guessing from GetAvailableCameras=0 alone. The SDK2 manual explicitly states GetAvailableCameras may be called before initialization, and for iDus GetCameraInformation(0, &info) is available specifically to report USB camera presence, DLL-load status, and camera-initialization status. A new diagnostic therefore compares these values before and after Initialize, then queries GetUSBDeviceDetails and GetVersionInfo after successful initialization. A separate PowerShell probe inspects the live Solis process modules and Windows Plug-and-Play/driver records so a path/version mismatch between Solis and the ctypes probe can be identified.

GitHub main was verified at commit aeca6f0995764b430bee7872b363893e7a4bf4f2, committed 2026-09-02 10:30:54 MDT. That commit intentionally removed the separate calibration reads/point control and made the existing repeats-per-point setting apply to both laser-calibration and power-dependent scans. This shared widget is a durable product decision and must not be reversed.

The working Andor camera library on the current 64-bit lab computer is C:\Program Files\Andor SOLIS\atmcd64d_legacy.dll. It enumerates DU401_BVF serial 26970 with a 1024 x 127 detector and 26 um pixels. C:\Program Files\Andor SOLIS\atmcd64d.dll loads but previously returned zero cameras. Kymera serial is KY-4444. The production adapter can connect and acquire when the legacy DLL is selected first.

Andor DLL discovery must distinguish an existing DLL from a functioning DLL. The current first-existing-file search is insufficient because both atmcd64d.dll and atmcd64d_legacy.dll exist while only the legacy library enumerates this iDus. Use explicit configuration plus functional fallback diagnostics rather than renaming or replacing installed Solis files.

Newport hot reconnect still fails on the lab computer after complete adapter teardown and five fresh construction attempts. The next discriminating test is same-process versus fresh-process recovery. If only a fresh process can reconnect, isolate Newport .NET control in a restartable helper process because a QThread cannot unload CLR/vendor static state.

User preference for diagnostics: expected missing/disconnected instruments and handled operation failures should be communicated primarily through GUI status or concise dialogs. Keep bounded rotating file logs available for diagnosis, but terminal warnings/errors should be uncommon and reserved for unexpected connection loss, internal defects, or uncaught failures rather than normal startup absence.

Preferred spectrometer startup behavior is explicit or automatic source selection among QEPro, Andor, emulator, and disconnected. The QEPro and Andor detector are normally mutually exclusive on USB, so auto mode should connect the single available configured backend quietly, start offline when none is present, and present a chooser only for ambiguity; post-start source changes remain available in Instrument Connections.

Laser selection should be an explicit session-only state, not QTableWidget current-row or hover state. Preferred UI: a small checkable selector at the left of every laser row, exactly zero or one active, clicking the active selector clears it, checking another transfers selection, and selection survives tab changes/measurements/edits/refresh but resets when the GUI exits.

Spectrum-file cleanup direction: add schema_version=2, keep a small always-present provenance core, and write power, scan/laser/filter, background, gated, and SNR metadata only when applicable. Do not indiscriminately delete requested_power_W, expected_actual_power_W, gated_sequence_id, gated_phase_index, or Newport status data because they are required for reconstructing the workflows that generate them. Eliminate duplicate notes_json and unrelated empty sentinel rows in new files while retaining backward-compatible loading.

Background compatibility should use an explicit policy. Strict mode requires matching backend/detector, calibration grid, ROI/binning, readout/amplifier, correction flags, averaging mode, and integration. A rate-scaled mode may permit different integration times only for a detector/workflow whose linearity and exposure-independent offsets have been validated. Canonical files should retain raw detector counts separately from processed display data.

Acquisition-layout direction: use a responsive two-column compact grid rather than dedicating a full row to integration, averages, boxcar width, and field. Future smoothing should expose a named method and width/parameters with a tiny kernel preview; smoothing is display/processing provenance and should not overwrite canonical raw counts by default.

Current gated timing is software-side. The reference transition timestamp is taken only after the OBIS set-enable command and immediate readback complete and the completion signal reaches the GUI thread. gated_request_elapsed_since_transition_ms is the request-emission time relative to that acknowledgement; acquisition call start/end are measured around the spectrometer adapter call, and midpoint is only their arithmetic mean. These values do not directly identify the physical laser transition or detector exposure. QEPro may return the most recently completed buffered spectrum, while Andor can be instrumented around StartAcquisition and verified with its FIRE output. Timing-critical work should use measured optical/TTL edges or a shared hardware trigger.

The 2026-09-02 validation candidate adds configurable legacy-first Andor SDK2 selection, an isolated DLL-matrix probe, Auto/QEPro/Andor/emulator/disconnected source selection, GUI-first handled errors with optional rotating logging, a restartable Newport CLR/vendor child process, QEPro completed-buffer draining plus one in-flight synchronization discard, an explicit session-only laser selector, compact acquisition/gated layouts, strict background signatures, spectrum schema v2, and exposure-aware gated timing quality control.

The Newport helper-process design is an implemented hypothesis awaiting the decisive lab power-cycle test. Startup uses one quick discovery attempt when the optional meter is absent; a manual Connect request performs five fresh spawned-process attempts with bounded re-enumeration delays. An operation timeout retires the entire helper so late RPC results cannot contaminate the next connection.

QEPro acquisition configuration now tracks integration time, device/software averaging state, and correction flags. On change, the adapter uses the exposed data_buffer clear or count/remove methods to discard all completed old frames, then consumes one possible in-flight frame before returning a measurement. This intentionally adds one unsaved synchronization exposure only after configuration changes and needs stable-lamp validation on QEP05831.

Spectrum schema v2 is implemented. New files always contain a small acquisition/identity core and adapter-output intensity column; a processed column appears only if GUI background subtraction or smoothing changed values. Power, operator, scan/laser/filter, background, gated, and SNR blocks are conditional. The loader continues to accept eager schema-v1 aliases, notes_json, active flags, intensity_counts, and headerless two-column files.

The current gated timing-quality implementation is an online robust compromise rather than full post-hoc spectral rejection. It prewarms the detector before a transition, schedules absolute perf_counter_ns deadlines, records controller and backend acquisition bounds/midpoints/uncertainty/per-average windows, classifies eligible OFF-frame residuals after a five-frame baseline, and defaults to discard with abort above 25 percent outliers after ten evaluated frames. This bounds memory for large decay plans; post-hoc or hybrid filtering remains a user decision.

Offline verification of the 2026-09-02 candidate under CPython 3.12 compiled all 132 Python files and passed 102 hardware-independent test invocations in a deterministic pytest-compatible runner. PySide6, pytest, Python 3.14, and vendor drivers were unavailable, so GUI construction, multiprocessing/pythonnet behavior, USB reconnect, actual detector buffer semantics, and physical timing remain bench-gated.

Source provenance caveat: the project ledger verified GitHub main aeca6f0995764b430bee7872b363893e7a4bf4f2 at the expected 10:30:54 MDT timestamp, but the private current GitHub tree could not be downloaded in the review environment. The candidate was built from the supplied 2026-08-27 reviewed source plus reconciled confirmed changes and must be diffed/merged against current main before lab replacement.

The answered product decisions are authoritative. Record field is checkbox-controlled and persisted; zero mT is valid; unchecked omits field metadata and filename use. File logging is bounded and enabled by default while normal expected hardware absence is GUI-only and console is ERROR-only. Background matching is strict. Normal Newport status is omitted and abnormal status retained. Acquisition layout keeps Exposure/Averages/Smoothing/Field/Live/Take/Background visible and moves secondary controls under Advanced. Smoothing supports None/Boxcar/Hann/Hamming/Gaussian/Triangle/Blackman/Cosine/Sine, selectable edge boundaries, an inline preview, and a detailed Fourier popup; Savitzky-Golay is later. Gated rejection is online/robust and bounded. Machine values belong in ignored config/lab_defaults.local.json.
The removed laser-calibration reads/point control must not be restored. One shared Repeats per point widget intentionally applies to laser calibration and power-dependent scans.

Magnetic-field applicability is represented as float-or-None throughout. Record field unchecked means None and omits the value from filenames/CSV; checked with 0.0 mT records a real zero. The GUI disables the numeric field control while recording is off.

Gated plan construction, preflight, and compact preview are now lazy. A 100000-frame plan builds without materializing actions, reports exact counts, and exposes only bounded preview rows. Safety guards reject more than 100000 frames, 250000 actions, or 5000 averaged traces and warn when estimated raw spectral storage exceeds 512 MiB.

Gated timing rejection uses an online robust rolling baseline after warm-up and does not retain full spectra. Eligible laser-OFF frames are classified by residual from rolling median using MAD/IQR scale, with detector exposure uncertainty as a minimum bound. The production policy automatically flags individual files and discards outliers from averaged outputs, separates baselines by backend and gated mode, warns without rejecting for stable bias, saves accepted partial averages on user abort, and records incomplete reason only for non-user failures. Hardware data must tune the numeric defaults.

Uploaded immediate-after-off gated timing files show nearly the same software scheduler latency: QEPro request 0.927 +/- 0.418 ms and call start 2.575 +/- 0.981 ms; Kymera request 0.959 +/- 0.306 ms and call start 2.749 +/- 0.933 ms. The QEPro call is about 7.72 ms while the Andor call is about 102.03 ms. Therefore roughly 94 ms of the performance gap is inside the current SDK2 acquisition path rather than Qt scheduling.

Andor SDK2 GetHSSpeed reports MHz. A displayed 0.1 MHz is 100 kHz, not 100 MHz, and matches the DU401 specification. GetVSSpeed reports microseconds per pixel; 8 us is the fastest clock while about 16 us is the quality-oriented Solis default. The adapter now chooses the closest 16 us vertical setting initially and labels both units explicitly.

Andor requested exposure and full-frame period are different quantities. After applying settings, query GetAcquisitionTimings and save the applied exposure; report minimum frame period/readout separately. The GUI allows short requests because SDK2 may apply them even when the full-frame period is longer; files preserve a differing request only when it does not match the applied exposure. Configuration changes invalidate prepared and continuous state. A blocked-light 1/5/10 ms matrix remains required before applying any configuration-specific lower guard.

The Solis-versus-GUI iDus throughput difference was confirmed to be acquisition mode. On DU401_BVF serial 26970, Run-Till-Abort sustained approximately 15.00 ms or 50.00 ms periods with sub-0.2 ms standard deviation, while re-armed acquisition took about 117-200 ms per frame and array transfer was below 0.1 ms. The GUI uses explicit Run-Till-Abort sessions for Live, gated, power-scan, and auto-tune acquisition; ordinary manual Take Spectrum remains single scan. No compilation or language rewrite is justified by these measurements.

Spectrum schema v4 groups closely related values, lets the recorded option encode feature enablement, omits normal power status and inactive workflow flags, preserves abnormal/status and reconstruction-critical scan/gated values conditionally, and remains backward-readable through schema v1 and plain two-column files. It adds approved software provenance, readback-confirmed Andor state, continuous-buffer evidence, selected Newport channel identities, strict background signature, smoothing boundary, pump/repetition gaps, and the same provenance in averaged gated output. docs/SPECTRUM_METADATA_SCHEMA_20260909.docx is the complete field/type/applicability/use/migration authority.

Plugins and user-defined procedures are feasible but were deliberately kept out of runtime code in this review. The recommended design is typed capability contracts plus a registry/manifest layer for trusted adapters/tools, a bounded declarative procedure DSL for routine workflows, and an optional local API for advanced VS Code/Jupyter clients. Laser authority, acquisition ownership, validation, cancellation, and audit trails stay in the host application.

Offline verification of the cumulative 2026-09-10 candidate under CPython 3.12 compiled all Python files and passed 131 hardware-independent test invocations in the deterministic compatibility runner before packaging. PySide6, pytest, Python 3.14, and vendor hardware were unavailable, so GUI construction, real acquisition performance, USB reconnect, physical timing, and camera-buffer semantics remain bench-gated.

The authoritative iDus probe geometry and speed list for this workstation is DU401_BVF serial 26970, 1024 by 127 pixels, 26 um pitch; horizontal clock values are 0.1, 0.05, and 0.033 MHz (100, 50, and 33 kHz), and vertical shifts are 8.25, 16.25, 32.25, and 64.25 us per pixel. The GUI defaults to the option nearest 16 us but exposes all returned choices.

Andor continuous acquisition is explicitly session-scoped. A compatible session arms SDK2 acquisition mode 5 once, removes frames already complete before each request, waits for the next frame, reads GetOldestImage in order, and records driver index, discarded backlog, and pending depth. Settings changes, owner changes, errors, disconnect, and shutdown stop the stream and restore single-scan/internal-trigger state. This requires bench validation against the actual SDK circular buffer before production use.

Andor close policy is guided warm-up: stop work and lasers, cooler OFF, query at a two-second cadence, block ordinary close until at least 0 C, and allow only a clearly confirmed emergency exit that leaves a persistent incomplete marker. Startup reports the marker but also queries the actual connected camera. The first-reading threshold is provisional pending lab/vendor guidance on a hold period.

Spectrum-time Newport measurement independently selects physical channel 1, channel 2, or both while leaving connection and live monitoring separate. Measure power requires at least one selected channel. Only selected channels are saved with explicit channel identities. Configurable repeated imbalance detection warns in status/logs but never changes the selected channel automatically.

Spectrum autosave now uses one serialized background executor so disk I/O cannot block the GUI thread and result ordering remains deterministic. Background subtraction is vectorized and detector/grid/settings signatures are cached. The historical approximately 0.5 Hz background regression still needs an instrument-side profile because vendor acquisition and filesystem costs cannot be reproduced offline.

Plugin and procedure decisions from QUESTIONS_20260909_answered.docx narrow but do not activate runtime extensibility: installation requires explicit administrative application mode plus OS permission; the first pilot is a read-only field sensor; authoring combines a schema-aware highlighted source editor, generated form, and emulator dry run; and contracts should be transport-neutral for eventual remote use. Procedure source syntax and the first external API deployment model remain open.

The complete 2026-09-11 lab log established that the Andor GUI failure was not a camera disconnect or exposure timeout. WaitForAcquisitionTimeOut returned DRV_SUCCESS, then GetOldestImage returned DRV_NO_NEW_DATA. This is consistent with an acquisition notification surviving the GUI freshness drain; a short event-to-buffer driver race has the same observable result. The tight-loop timing probe did not create this inter-request condition, and both interpretations require treating the unread buffer range as authoritative.

Andor continuous readiness now requires a non-empty GetNumberNewImages range. After draining frames completed before a GUI request, successful but stale acquisition-event wakes are ignored within one original timeout; GetOldestImage is called only after unread data are confirmed. The adapter records stale_wait_notifications in diagnostic stage timing. troubleshooting.andor_stream_gap_probe reproduces GUI pauses and reports completion, driver indices, discarded frames, and stale events without saving spectra. The focused fake-native regression passes; physical multi-frame confirmation remains the highest-priority gate.

Offline verification of the focused 2026-09-11 candidate under CPython 3.12 compiled and statically checked 140 Python files and passed 132 hardware-independent test invocations. The regression suite explicitly covers a drained frame whose stale SDK event wakes before the next real image. PySide6, Python 3.14, atmcd64d_legacy.dll, and physical hardware remain unavailable in the review runtime, so the stream-gap probe and GUI multi-frame paths are still bench gates.

The second 2026-09-11 lab pass confirms the stale-event Run-Till-Abort correction on the production iDus: the gap probe completed 100/100 requests at 15 ms with 100 ms pauses, indices increased monotonically from 1 to 694, 594 pre-request frames were discarded, and 99 stale notifications were recovered. GUI Live at 15 and 50 ms and multi-frame gated acquisition also completed. Power-scan, auto-tune, explicit multi-average, stop/cancel/reconnect, and deliberate-overflow cases remain part of the broader owner regression.

The negative Kymera gated midpoint values are real selection bias, not timer-reset or save-order artifacts. Across 0, 150, 300, 450, and 600 ms targets, estimated exposure midpoints were consistently 9.4 to 11.5 ms early because the first frame completing readout after a request could have been exposed before the requested midpoint. Gated OFF-frame acquisition now passes an absolute monotonic midpoint target to SDK2 and consumes early frames until the first estimated midpoint-eligible frame; target-alignment discards are stored separately from the pre-request backlog.

Gated timing policy remains exposure-midpoint based. At a zero-millisecond delay, a valid accepted exposure can begin before laser OFF when it straddles the transition, but its estimated midpoint must not precede the target. Software estimates remain bounded evidence rather than physical-trigger truth; a camera FIRE or shared trigger measurement is required before claiming tighter temporal accuracy.

Andor Spectrometer Details settings are now explicit transactions rather than passive editable widgets. Apply and verify sends one payload through MainWindow, InstrumentRuntime, and the device worker; the composite adapter stops streaming, validates before mutation, applies camera and Kymera changes in dependency order, waits for available motion readback, refreshes calibration and capabilities, and returns success/failure to the dialog. The companion controls probe is read-only by default and restores test changes unless explicitly told to retain them.

The iDus TEC target is cached after a successful native command and reloaded into Spectrometer Details for the remainder of the connected GUI session. This fixes the visual reset without adding continuous camera queries. The duplicate cooler exit warning, theme-restart interaction, and emergency-exit dialog ordering remain the next functional UI fix after hardware validation of settings and midpoint selection.

The 2026-09-11 lab pass also confirmed Newport reconnection after a power cycle, expected unavailable-instrument startup states in the GUI status bar without terminal warnings, and background subtraction at approximately the same visible rate as unsubtracted Live acquisition. Missing-local-config clarity and the checked-without-an-in-memory-background presentation remain UX tasks.

Offline verification of the cumulative 2026-09-11 revision under CPython 3.12 compiled and statically checked 141 Python files and passed 137 hardware-independent test invocations. Tests cover gated absolute midpoint forwarding, early-frame rejection, pending-frame dating, target-discard metadata, transactional Andor control ordering/readback failure, controls-probe import safety, and all prior regressions. PySide6, Python 3.14, atmcd64d_legacy.dll, and physical hardware remain unavailable here, so the aligned timing and control-application checks remain bench gates.

The complete andor_probe_results_20260914.zip passed CRC/path-safety checks and every value was parsed: 13 JSON files and eight schema-v4 gated CSVs with all metadata, trace, and 1024-point data rows. Grating, center wavelength, filter, flipper, horizontal speed, vertical speed, and available gain changes applied and restored. FVB binning 4 returned DRV_NOT_SUPPORTED; focus 423 to 400 returned ATSPECTROGRAPH_P2INVALID.

The 2026-09-14 unaligned and midpoint-aligned Andor gap probes each completed 100/100 requests. Unaligned: 595 pre-request discards, zero target discards, 99 stale notifications, steady-state call median 4.367 ms, and all 99 exposure midpoints early with median -16.562 ms. Aligned: 594 pre-request discards, 198 target discards, 99 stale notifications, call median 34.353 ms, and all 99 midpoint-eligible with median +13.425 ms. The extra wait is deliberate eligibility selection, not stream re-arming.

Current gated timing semantics: the transition origin is timestamped in the GUI after the OBIS set command and AM:STATe? readback complete; it is not an optical edge. Request is coordinator emission time. Acquisition-call bounds surround the worker's adapter call and exclude later plot/save work. Exposure bounds are backend estimates; Andor reconstructs them from SDK-applied exposure/readout/cycle timing. Timing error is signed selected exposure reference minus requested delay, while exposure uncertainty is a conservative bound rather than a standard deviation.

Negative exposure-start values at zero delay are valid when a finite exposure straddles the software transition origin and its selected midpoint is eligible. In the eight supplied GUI CSVs, negative means/minima occurred only for zero-delay exposure start; request, call, accepted exposure-midpoint, and timing-error means were nonnegative. Negative request/call values or negative selected-reference error under a strict nonnegative policy would require investigation.

Retain N inside fixed window is implemented for averaged delayed-after-OFF and interleaved-decay runs. Repeats is the accepted count per trace. The user selects exposure start or midpoint, symmetric tolerance, and a finite attempt multiplier. Rejected arrays are released; accepted frames update incremental mean/variance; satisfied traces are skipped; a partial schema-v5 series with reason is saved if the ceiling is exhausted. Per-frame Newport reads and individual output are disabled to protect timing and file volume.

Fixed-window retention constrains recorded software estimates, not physical laser timing. A narrow +/-2 ms window can have low yield with an approximately 15 ms free-running iDus period, and serial command/readback latency is not optical truth. Production calibration should compare each OBIS channel's optical OFF edge with a fast photodiode/DAQ or characterized trigger/FIRE signal before assigning a physical tolerance.

For low-emissivity phosphorescence, prioritize photon collection and controlled backgrounds before software enhancement: optimize sample/slit imaging and numerical aperture, widen slit within resolution needs, select grating/blaze/port, remove unnecessary losses, cool/stabilize detector, characterize gain/readout, lengthen pump/exposure, and average accepted cycles. A future phase-cycled boxcar mode should pair pump/reference frames and propagate variance; template or wavelength-band estimators may follow, while raw evidence remains preserved.
